source: KSQAAC Spardha Yashassu NMMS Study Material 2022, MAT Chapter 11 (questions: PDF pages 39-43, answers: PDF page 126). The pictures are cropped with tools/figures/ch11.json. Every answer is worked out from the faces in the pictures (views tried on every possible die, nets folded in 3D) in tools/check_dice.ts.

questions.prompt: Two positions of the same dice are given. Which number is opposite to 6?
questions.rule: 3 is on top in both views, so turn the dice about 3: going clockwise round 3, the first view reads 6, 1 and the second 5, 2. The four faces round 3 run 6, 1, 5, 2, and faces two apart are opposite.
questions.working: Round 3: 6 → 1 → 5 → 2. So 6 is opposite 5, and 1 is opposite 2.

questions.prompt: Three positions of the same dice are given below. Find the number opposite to 5.
questions.rule: A face can't be seen together with its opposite face. List every face seen next to 5; the one never seen with it is opposite.
questions.working: Next to 5: 3 and 6 (first view), 2 and 4 (second view). The only face left is 1, so 1 is opposite 5.

questions.prompt: Two positions of the same dice are given. Which letter will be opposite to the letter B?
questions.rule: C is on the right in both views, so the dice was turned about C. The faces round C then keep their order: top B, front F in one view; top A, front E in the other. Round C they run B, F, A, E, and faces two apart are opposite.
questions.working: Round C: B → F → A → E. So B is opposite A, and F is opposite E.

questions.prompt: Three positions of the same dice are given. Observe them carefully. Which colour will be opposite to Black?
questions.rule: A face can't be seen together with its opposite face. List every colour seen next to Black; the one never seen with it is opposite.
questions.working: Next to Black: Yellow and Pink (first view), Orange and Blue (second view). The only colour left is Green, so Green is opposite Black.
questions.note: The first two views are enough. The third is drawn the wrong way round for them (Pink and Green should swap sides), but that doesn't change the answer.

questions.prompt: Three positions of the same dice are given. How many dots are there on the face opposite to the six dots?
questions.rule: Count the dots on each face first. Then find every face seen next to 5: the one never seen with it is its opposite.
questions.working: The views show (top, left, right) 2, 4, 5 · 5, 3, 1 · 4, 1, 6. Next to 5: 2, 4, 3 and 1. The only face left is 6, so 6 dots are opposite 5 dots.
questions.note: The first two views are enough. The third can't be the same dice as drawn (the first two put 4 opposite 1, yet it shows 4 and 1 together), but that doesn't change the answer.

questions.prompt: Four positions of the same dice are given. Which of the following is opposite to V?
questions.rule: III is seen next to II, I, V and IV, so III's opposite is the sixth face, which is never shown. V is seen next to I, III and IV; it can't be opposite the sixth face (that one belongs to III), so V must be opposite the face left over.
questions.working: Next to V: I, III, IV. Opposite III: the unseen face. Left over for V: II.

questions.prompt: This open dice is folded into a cube. What will be the number opposite to 6?
questions.rule: In a straight line of squares, the 1st and 3rd are opposite (one square between them). The column reads 3, 6, 2, 4.
questions.working: 3 and 2 are opposite, 6 and 4 are opposite (and 5 and 1 are opposite).

questions.prompt: In the following open dice, how many dots are there on the face opposite to the four dots?
questions.rule: In a straight line of squares, the 1st and 3rd are opposite. The top row reads 4, 1, 3.
questions.note: Hidden: the two rows of the drawing touch only at a corner, so it can't be folded into a cube as printed, and options A and D are both printed as 5. The book's answer, 3, comes from the top row alone.

questions.prompt: In the given open dice, what will be the letter opposite to M?
questions.rule: In a straight line of squares, the 1st and 3rd are opposite. The column reads Q, M, R, P.
questions.working: Q and R are opposite, M and P are opposite (and O and N are opposite).

questions.prompt: This open dice is folded into a cube. Which sign is opposite to the sign *?
questions.rule: The column reads +, ×, −, ÷, so + is opposite −, and × is opposite ÷. That leaves * and =.
questions.working: Fold with × at the bottom: * folds up on the left and = (next to −, which is the front) folds up on the right. So * is opposite =.

questions.prompt: Observe the following figure, and find what is opposite to 10.
questions.rule: With 10 as the floor, the squares 40, 50, 30 and 20 fold up into the four walls of a box with no lid. The four triangles on their outer edges then fold in over the open top and meet in a point, like a roof.
questions.working: Opposite 10 is the roof made of the four triangles: +, −, × and ÷.

questions.prompt: Identify the correct dice for the given figure.
questions.rule: First find the opposite pairs: the column N, P, Q, R gives N–Q and P–R, and M and O, on either side of N, are opposite. Opposite faces can never be seen together.
questions.working: A shows M and O, B shows N and Q, D shows P and R, all opposite pairs. Only C (N, R, O) has no opposite pair.
questions.note: Hidden: no option is exactly right. C, the book's key, is the only one with no opposite pair, but folding the net puts O on the left and R on the right when N is on top; C has them the other way round, as in a mirror.

questions.prompt: Identify the general dice in the given figure.
questions.rule: In a standard dice the opposite faces add up to 7 (1–6, 2–5, 3–4), so two faces that add up to 7 are never seen together. The book calls a dice where two touching faces add up to 7 a general dice.
questions.working: C shows 1 and 6 side by side: 1 + 6 = 7, so it can't be a standard dice. A (2, 3, 6), B (1, 2, 3) and D (4, 5, 1) have no two faces adding up to 7.

questions.prompt: Pairs of opposite faces of this dice are given below. Which of the following is not a right pair?
questions.rule: In the column (triangle, parallelogram, circle, diamond) the 1st and 3rd are opposite, and so are the 2nd and 4th. The right triangle and the hexagon, on either side, are opposite each other.
questions.working: Opposite pairs: triangle–circle, parallelogram–diamond, right triangle–hexagon. The circle and the parallelogram are next to each other in the column, so D is not a pair.

questions.prompt: Two positions of the same dice are given. Identify the right pairs of opposite faces.
questions.rule: Faces seen together are never opposite. 6 is seen with 1, 4, 3 and 2, so 6 is opposite 5. Then 1 is seen with 4 and 6, and turning the second view so that 6 matches gives 1 opposite 2 and 4 opposite 3.
questions.working: B, C and D pair 4 with 6 or 1 with 6, which are seen together. Only A is left: (4, 3) (1, 2) (6, 5).
